bibliography.corrections: entry is incomplete; it should read: Steinhart, G. B., Dunlop, E. S., Ridgway, M. S. & Marschall, E. A. 2008. Should I stay or should I go? Optimal parental care decisions of a nest-guarding fish. Evolutionary Ecology Research 10: 351-371. (Journal and pages match.)

claims.claim: Daily survival within guarded broods is about 0.90 for embryos and 0.92 for larvae
claims.quote: Base offspring daily survival rate (DSR) was 0.9 for embryos
claims.conditions: base inputs of a stochastic dynamic programming model, embryos on days 1-13 and larvae on days 14-20 of care, the same in Lake Erie and Lake Opeongo, 'based on values from Lake Opeongo and elsewhere (Friesen, 1998; Knotek and Orth, 1998)'; varied by ± 0.05 in the sensitivity runs
claims.note: the sentence continues 'and 0.92 for larvae (d = 14-20)'. These are model parameters taken from field studies, not new measurements: the primary sources are Friesen 1998 and Knotek & Orth 1998.

claims.claim: Smallmouth bass, Opeongo and other waters: Z 0.105 (guarded embryos), 0.083 (guarded larvae)
claims.note: Z = −ln(0.90) = 0.1054 and −ln(0.92) = 0.0834 per day: the conversion is right (project arithmetic)

notes: Only the bibliography needs completing. Table 2 also gives the daily probability that a nest is destroyed by a storm (0.065 Lake Erie, 0.015 Lake Opeongo), the values the paper cites to Steinhart 2004. Result useful for the egg stage: adult annual survival was the strongest factor in males' abandonment thresholds; storms, angling and nest predators raised the brood size below which males abandon.
